items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the public authorities law, in relation to requiring a safety briefing of Metro-North commuter railroad passengers to be conducted at each departure and every twenty minutes thereafter
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S4178

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the public authorities law, in
relation to requiring a safety briefing of Metro-North commuter
railroad passengers to be conducted at each departure and every twenty
minutes thereafter

PURPOSE:

Directs the metropolitan transportation authority to provide safety
briefings to passengers aboard Metro-North trains, and instruct
personnel in safety procedures

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one of the bill amends the public authorities law by adding a
new section 1279-d, which directs the authority to implement a safety
briefing to passengers no later than January 1, 2016.

Such plan shall include, but not be limited to:

-Before each departure, and every twenty minutes thereafter, the
conductor shall communicate when, where and under what circumstances
smoking is prohibited; in 0 - Evacuation procedures;
- Location and means for opening the passenger entry doors and
emergency exits;
- Location of survival equipment; and
- Location and operation of fire extinguishers.

The briefings may be delivered by an approved recording playback
devise. The plan shall also provide for the training of conductors,
trainmen and other designated employees in emergency techniques and
procedures, interoperable communications, and knowledge of procedures
and equipment used during evacuations.

Section two states the effective date.

JUSTIFICATION:

On February 3, 2015, during the evening rush hour, the northbound
Metro-North Railroad passenger train no. 659 impacted with a sports
utility vehicle which had stopped on the tracks at the Commerce Street
highway rail grade crossing. This tragic accident resulted in the
deaths of five passengers seated in the lead passenger railcar and the
driver of the sports utility vehicle. Although the National
Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) is currently investigating this
horrific accident, many passengers reported much confusion and
difficulty in evacuating the damaged train.

In March of 2014, the Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) issued a
report to Congress evaluating the safety measures of the Metro-North
system. In the report, the FRA strongly urged the senior leadership of
Metro-North to prioritize safety, and implement a plan to improve
safety standards and procedures. Unlike the Metropolitan Transit
Authority's (MTA) notification announcements on the New York City
subway system, Metro-North does not provide routine briefings to
passengers regarding proper evacuation and safety procedures. This


lack of instruction resulted in much confusion to the roughly 650
passengers on the train at the time of the Valhalla crash. Therefore,
it would be in the interest of public safety to require Metro-North
Railroad Safety Committee to utilize and disseminate similar
information as is provided on the City's subway system.

In emergency situations, passengers cannot be reasonably expected to
know the exact location of fire extinguishers, emergency exits and
other pertinent information without repetition. By requiring this
information be disseminated upon the departure of each train, as well
as every twenty minutes thereafter, over-time, New York's commuters
will become better aware of proper emergency procedures, which will
save the lives of future passengers should another tragedy occur.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None

EFFECTIVE DATE:

This act shall take effect immediately.

B.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S4178B

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the public authorities law, in
relation to requiring a safety briefing of Metro-North commuter
railroad passengers to be conducted at certain times

 PURPOSE :

Directs the metropolitan transportation authority to provide safety
briefings to passengers aboard Metro-North trains, and instruct
personnel in safety procedures

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section one of the bill amends the public authorities law by adding a
new section I279-d, which directs the authority to implement a safety
briefing to passengers no later than January 1, 2017 for persons
utilizing transportation and other related services of the Metro-North
commuter railroad.

Such program shall include, but not be limited to: before initial
departure of each train, and periodically thereafter, at the
discretion of the authority at stations where the greatest number of
passengers board the train, the conductor, or the conductor's
designee, shall immediately communicate live and/or by recorded,
visual and/or audio images: evacuation procedures; location and means
for opening the passenger entry doors and emergency exits; location of
first aid and survival equipment and location and operation of fire
extinguishers. Additionally, in the event of a disaster or emergency,
the conductor, or the conductor's designee shall communicate the
safety briefing message as often as necessary to ensure passenger
safety.

The briefings may be delivered by an approved recording playback
devise. The plan shall also provide for the training of conductors,
trainmen and other designated employees in emergency techniques and
procedures, interoperable communications, and knowledge of procedures
and equipment used during evacuations.

Section two states the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

On February 3, 2015, during the evening rush hour, the northbound
Metro-North Railroad passenger train no. 659 impacted with a sports
utility vehicle which had stopped on the tracks at the Commerce Street
highway rail grade crossing. This tragic accident resulted in the
deaths of five passengers seated in the lead passenger railcar and the
driver of the sports utility vehicle. Although the National
Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) is currently investigating this
horrific accident, many passengers reported much confusion and
difficulty in evacuating the damaged train.

In March of 2014, the Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) issued a
report to Congress evaluating the safety measures of the Metro-North
system. In the report, the FRA strongly urged the senior leadership of
Metro-North to prioritize safety, and implement a plan to improve
safety standards and procedures. Unlike the Metropolitan Transit
Authority's (MTA) notification announcements on the New York City
subway system, Metro-North does not provide routine briefings to
passengers regarding proper evacuation and safety procedures. This
lack of instruction resulted in much confusion to the roughly 650
passengers on the train at the time of the Valhalla crash. Therefore,
it would be in the interest of public safety to require Metro-North
Railroad Safety Committee to utilize and disseminate similar
information as is provided on the City's subway system.
In emergency situations, passengers cannot be reasonably expected to
know the exact location of fire extinguishers, emergency exits and
other pertinent information without repetition. By requiring this
information be disseminated upon the initial departure of each train,
as well as at stations where the greatest number of passengers board
the train, over-time, New York's commuters will become better aware of
proper emergency procedures, which will save the lives of future
passengers should another tragedy occur.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

New bill

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately.
